title: The Barrens
body: The Barrens is a vast savanna of red earth, yellow grass and thorny scrub in the heart of Kalimdor, stretching from the forests of Ashenvale in the north to the canyons of Thousand Needles in the south, with Durotar across the river to the east and Mulgore beyond the hills to the west. Long ago it was woodland tended by the night elves, until the Burning Legion, war and the Sundering left it scorched and dry. In recent years new oases have formed, fed by some power seeping up from below, and the life they bring is not wholly natural. The Horde holds the Crossroads where the great roads meet, the tauren keep Camp Taurajo, and orc posts watch the borders at Far Watch and Mor'shan. Kolkar centaurs, Razormane and Bristleback quilboar and Witchwing harpies all contest the land. Goblins run the free port of Ratchet while the Venture Company drills in the north, Theramore's soldiers hold Northwatch on the coast, dwarves dig at Bael Modan, and silithid swarm in the Field of Giants.

title: Far Watch Post
body: Far Watch Post is the orc garrison that guards the Barrens end of the bridge over the Southfury River, the first stop on the western road out of Razor Hill. Kargal Battlescar commands it, signing the letters of young conscripts sent over from Durotar and passing them on to the Crossroads, where, he grumbles, the real need lies. Two others keep company with him. Ak'Zeloth, assistant to the warlock Neeru Fireblade of Orgrimmar, keeps a table of flawed power stones close at hand, readied for a task on Dreadmist Peak, and just to the south the veteran Uzzek, a fighter of many battles, drills young warriors in the art of defense.

title: Dreadmist Peak
body: Dreadmist Peak rises from the plains north of the Crossroads, and the safest way to its summit lies up the northern face. Cultists of the Burning Blade have made it their own. Bruisers and acolytes of the cult guard its slopes, and among them, seldom seen, walks Rathorian, a felguard demon. In a cave near the top, the Dreadmist Den, the Demon Seed rests above a demonic altar of fire: an object of power around which the cult rallies, and a tool of the Burning Legion itself. Not every tenant of the peak belongs to the cult. An undead mage, Sarilus Foulborne, keeps to the heights alone.

title: Grol'dom Farm
body: Grol'dom Farm is a small orc homestead north of the Crossroads, on the road that leads toward the night elf forests. It is a family place. Karu cooks roasted plainstrider over the fire and wonders why the pigs were never fed, Trok runs in circles trying to escape a swarm of angry bees, and young Okla begs her father for leave to gather pretty stones for a necklace, with a sharp one saved for her friend Gruk's spear. Her father is Kranal Fiss, and he is more than a farmer. Young shamans of the Horde are sent to his door when they are ready to learn the ways of fire.

title: Thorn Hill
body: Northeast of the Crossroads, where great thorny vines thrust up out of the earth, the Razormane quilboar have dug their dens. The thorns mark the quilboar wherever they settle, and from Thorn Hill the Razormane strike at the caravans that carry supplies along the road from Durotar, leaving stolen crates of the Crossroads' goods strewn through their camps. Water seekers, thornweavers, geomancers and defenders crowd the hill under the eye of Elder Mystic Razorsnout, and Thork's scouts name the raider Kreenig Snarlsnout as the one leading the attacks. They have not spared the hermit smith on the hills nearby either: an iron chest stolen from his camp lies among their huts.

title: The Crossroads
body: The Crossroads is the largest Horde town in the Barrens, a walled outpost raised where the great roads of the Barrens cross. Thork leads its defenses in the Warchief's name, and the shaman Sergra Darkthorn sets newcomers to work. Raids on its caravans keep the garrison busy, and the town is full of tasks: Darsok Swiftdagger wants harpies dead, Gazrog wants back the guards' silver payroll, stolen by raptors of all things, and the troll Korran studies the strange insects of the south for his masters in Orgrimmar. The Forsaken apothecary Helbrim works among the tents, the druid Tonga Runetotem ponders the oases, and the grieving warrior Mankrik watches the horizon from dawn till dusk.

title: The Dry Hills
body: The Dry Hills climb toward the mountains in the northwest of the Barrens, and they belong to the Witchwing harpies. The harpies are not native to these plains: they came down from Stonetalon, far to the northwest, and they have been ravaging the Horde's caravan supplies for a long time. Their flock keeps a strict order. Harpies and roguefeathers make up the lower ranks, windcallers and ambushers fly among them, and the slayers serve as lieutenants, each marked by a ring she carries. Above them all is Serena Bloodfeather, whose raids are revenge for a sister slain by Rexxar, and a harpy called Sister Rathtalon is sometimes seen hunting the hills.

title: The Forgotten Pools
body: Northwest of the Crossroads lie the Forgotten Pools, one of the oases that have formed in the Barrens in recent years. The druid Tonga Runetotem senses a power leaking up to the surface of this dry land, and he suspects these waters may hold its source. The life here has its oddities. Laden mushrooms grow by the water, their spores prized by the apothecaries of the Forsaken, and strange deviate fish swim in the pools. Kolkar centaurs, wranglers and stormers, keep camp along the banks, and the Kolkar leader Barak Kodobane has made his camp near the pools.

title: The Mor'shan Rampart
body: In the far north of the Barrens, where the grass gives way to the forests of Ashenvale, the Horde has raised the Mor'shan Rampart, a fortified wall and watch tower to hold the border against the night elves. Barrens guards keep the gate. Kadrak commands from the tower and leads the Horde's campaign in Ashenvale, sending fresh recruits on to the new outposts at Splintertree and the Zoram Strand and runners with fresh orders to his Warsong scouts. He will not suffer Alliance messengers to cross Horde ground. Just to the south, the goblin tinkerer Wenikee Boltbucket keeps a camp, ready to take apart any machine that catches her eye.

title: The Sludge Fen
body: The Sludge Fen is a fouled stretch of the northern Barrens where the Venture Company works its derricks. Drudgers and mercenaries swarm the site under Supervisor Lugwizzle, shredders lumber about, and tool buckets lie everywhere, stocked with the company's nugget slugs. The rivals of Ratchet watch it closely: one goblin spy climbed into a stolen shredder here only to find he had no key. North of the fen stands a Venture Co. tower, southwest of it a small research site guards a device called the samophlange, and to the northeast the company's Boulder Lode Mine is worked by overseers and enforcers, where a miner is rumored to have dug up an emerald the size of a fist.

title: Ratchet
body: Ratchet is the goblin port on the eastern coast of the Barrens, founded by Gazlowe with the pay Thrall gave him for building Orgrimmar. It is a town of the Steamwheedle Cartel and open to all who trade in peace, and the boat Maiden's Fancy carries its cargo and passengers across the sea to Booty Bay. Everyone here has a scheme. Wharfmaster Dizzywig keeps the ledgers of every crate, Sputtervalve of the Tinkers' Union runs a shredder program, Mebok Mizzyrix brews smart drinks, Brewmaster Drohn keeps the old recipes of Chen Stormstout, and the high elf Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun leads the Thalo'dan Privateers. A small coven of warlocks makes its home here too.

title: The Tidus Stair
body: Along the shore south of Ratchet, beyond the mouth of the Southfury, the tauren shaman Islen Waterseer keeps a fishing hut. She is a teacher of water. Young shamans of the Horde are sent to her when their spirits are warmed by fire, and even outsiders come to her from lands as far off as Felwood, seeking her friendship with the spirits of water. Beside her camps Mahren Skyseer, sister of Jorn of Camp Taurajo, who hunts the great beasts of the sea along this coast and takes on any hunter her brother has judged worthy.

title: The Merchant Coast
body: South of Ratchet the shore runs on as the Merchant Coast, and the trade it was named for now has to sail past pirates. The Southsea Freebooters have set up a camp here, almost on Gazlowe's doorstep, and their brigands and cannoneers guard strongboxes full of plunder taken from goblin ships: crates of boots from Booty Bay, a lens for Gazlowe's observatory and other stolen goods lie among their tents. Their captain, Baron Longshore of Gilneas, commands the ship called the Heedless and has a price on his head. Their ship, the Tide Razor, lies along this coast too, with a den aboard where they train their thieves, and makrura and sand sharks haunt the shallows.

title: Fray Island
body: Fray Island lies off the Merchant Coast, reached by wading the sand bar shallows, and it is a place where warriors meet to fight one another. Its chief warrior is the human Klannoc Macleod, called the Islander, who welcomes rising fighters of any people. Those who want his teaching must first pass the Affray. At its heart the challenger steps onto a grate before a crowd of cheering spectators, and the goblin announcer Twiggy Flathead calls out challenger after challenger, until at last he sends in Big Will. Only one who beats them all in the time allowed earns Klannoc's respect, and with it the berserker's way.

title: Northwatch Hold
body: Northwatch Hold is a human fortress on the coast south of Ratchet, built by survivors of the Alliance expedition and held now by marines and preservers of Theramore, blocking the coastal road toward Dustwallow Marsh. Captain Fairmount commands it with her cannoneers Whessan and Smythe, and their guns have sunk so many ships that Captain Brightsun of Ratchet calls them overzealous, trigger happy louts. They hold at least one prisoner: Gilthares Firebough, a deckhand on a moonshine run who was branded a threat to the Alliance. The waters offshore belong to Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, a sea beast the humans on this coast have every reason to fear.

title: Lushwater Oasis
body: Lushwater Oasis lies south of the Crossroads, one of the green pools that have sprung up across the plains, and beneath it opens the mouth of the Wailing Caverns. The druid Naralex went down into those caverns hoping to dream the Barrens green again, and his dream turned to nightmare. His few faithful disciples keep watch near the entrance, asking travelers to cull the deviate beasts that crawl from below. Above ground the oasis belongs to the Kolkar. Hezrul Bloodmark, leader of all the Kolkar centaurs in the Barrens, commands his people from here and berates them to look fierce, while snapjaw turtles altered by the water lurk at the shore.

title: The Stagnant Oasis
body: Southeast of the Crossroads lies the Stagnant Oasis, its waters as still as its name. The Kolkar have pitched a command tent here, and bloodchargers, marauders and pack runners with their hounds guard it, alongside two notorious brutes, Brokespear and Rocklance. The dervish Verog wanders the plains from this camp, and when the centaurs are pressed hard enough they raise an alarm and he comes, calling challengers to his tent to die. Like the other new oases, its still water may hide the source of the life returning to the Barrens. Sunscale raptors nest to the southwest.

title: Camp Taurajo
body: Camp Taurajo is the tauren outpost of the southern Barrens, standing on the road east from Mulgore where young tauren first come down from their homeland. Kirge Sternhorn senses a foul wind blowing from the east, and he sends the newly arrived north to the Crossroads, for the lives of the tauren and the orcs are now intertwined. The hunter Jorn Skyseer guides those who walk his path, Ruga Ragetotem sets warriors a trial among the silithid, and the orc smith Tatternack Steelforge studies the crude weapons of the quilboar for the Warchief. The camp's strangest resident is a prisoner: the caged Razormane Mangletooth, who has information to sell.

title: Agama'gor and Bramblescar
body: North of Camp Taurajo, giant thorns burst from the earth at Agama'gor and Bramblescar, and here the Bristleback quilboar keep their camps. To the quilboar such thorns are holy, for they grew where the blood of their boar god Agamaggan fell, and the Bristlebacks dig blood red shards from the ground among them to carry as totems of strength and magic. Hunters and water seekers fill the camps, while thornweavers and geomancers gather at Bramblescar. The Bristlebacks are bitter rivals of the Razormane, and bitter enemies of the Horde: an orc grunt named Dogran was taken captive at Agama'gor after a raid on their huts went wrong.

title: Field of Giants
body: South of Camp Taurajo spreads the Field of Giants, where great mounds of earth rise from the grass and something has come that does not belong. Silithid have made their hives here: creepers, swarmers and grubs pour from the mounds, and a huge harvester stalks among them, a creature that seems to stand outside the natural order. The insects are new to the Barrens, and those who watch them are uneasy. They show more wit than any beast should, Korran of the Crossroads thinks, and his reports have reached Orgrimmar. Ruga Ragetotem dislikes what they herald.

title: Blackthorn Ridge
body: Blackthorn Ridge lies deep in the south of the Barrens, beyond the Field of Giants, and it is Razormane country. Seers, stalkers, pathfinders and warfrenzied warriors of the tribe crowd its thorny slopes, and though the tribe has no skilled smiths, word has it they have begun to make sturdier weapons. Three of them stand out, Nak, Kuz and Lok Orcbane, a caster, a tracker and a warrior, and a brute named Hagg Taurenbane prowls among the camps. Yet someone lives here by choice: the orc shaman Brine keeps a lonely hut on the ridge, beside a watering hole the quilboar guard like treasure.

title: Bael Modan
body: South of the Field of Giants, the dwarves of Ironforge have torn open the earth at Bael Modan. Excavators and foremen blast deep holes into the ground with explosives and noisy machines, a flying machine stands over the dig, and the fortress of Bael'dun Keep, built to guard the site, now bristles with riflemen, soldiers and officers under General Twinbraid. The land was not empty. Tauren of the Stonespire tribe once lived here, and many were killed or driven off when the dwarves came. The dig's first great find, a gem called the Tear of the Moons, was locked away as cursed after it drove the dwarf Feegly mad.

title: The Razorfen
body: In the far south of the Barrens, near the edge of the Thousand Needles, rise the Razorfen, the greatest of all the thorn clusters. The quilboar hold that they are the very body of Agamaggan, their boar god, who fell in the War of the Ancients, and that the entrance to the Razorfen Downs is his great maw, which swallows any who are disloyal to him. In Razorfen Kraul the crone Charlga Razorflank musters a foul army, and the tauren Auld Stonespire of Thunder Bluff wants her heart for driving his people from their holy land. At the Downs a night elf watcher has seen something worse: an undead diplomat granting undeath to quilboar who beg for power.

title: Thork
body: Thork is the orc who leads the defenses of the Crossroads in the Warchief's name, and he welcomes newcomers so long as they mind their business. He has plenty to defend against. Razormane raids on the caravans from Durotar starve the town of supplies, and while his scouts hunt for whoever leads them, he sets the young to thin the quilboar, kill the raider Kreenig Snarlsnout and recover what was stolen. Thork greets tauren sent from Camp Taurajo as allies and points eager recruits north to the Ashenvale front, but grieving Mankrik he turns away, saying rage clouds his judgment.

title: Sergra Darkthorn
body: Sergra Darkthorn is the orc shaman in charge of the Crossroads, and she makes it plain that she tolerates no insolence: Thrall himself, she reminds the young, has set the Horde's women on equal footing with its men. Kargal Battlescar of Far Watch grumbles that she will talk a recruit's head in circles, though Thrall is convinced she is something special. To young hunters she is a first guide, sending them after plainstriders, zhevra, prowlers and the great white cat Echeyakee. She teaches that there is more to hunting than finding and killing, and at last she sends them to lay the feathers of slain raptors on the scytheclaw nests, to show those beasts they are not feared.

title: Gazlowe
body: Gazlowe is the goblin who rules Ratchet. A goblin of Undermine and a member of the Steamwheedle Cartel, he served Thrall as chief engineer of Durotar, and with the gold the Warchief paid him for Orgrimmar he founded his own port in the Barrens. He keeps it open to anyone with coin and on good terms with the Horde. Business would be perfect but for the Southsea Freebooters, who raid his ships, camp on his doorstep and have stolen everything from his boots to the lens for his observatory, and he complains that the trade princes' fleets do too little about it. He has put a bounty on the head of their captain, Baron Longshore.

She held three of them off alone, but more came, and when he turned in rage to face them, he was overwhelmed. A tauren druid found him lying on the Gold Road and tended his wounds. Now he stands at the Crossroads from sunrise to sunset scanning the horizon, killing every quilboar he meets and asking for their tusks.

He claims to know who truly leads the raids on the Horde, and he will tell for a price: blows against the Bristlebacks' spiritual leaders. He tells of Agamaggan, whose blood raised the thorns of the Barrens, and he still knows the old quilboar magic: bring him the blood shards the Bristlebacks carry, and he will bless the bearer with the boar god's strength, speed or spirit.

title: Jorn Skyseer
body: Jorn Skyseer is the tauren hunter of Camp Taurajo who teaches that, though others call this land barren, it teems with life for one who knows where to look. He takes up the training of young hunters after Sergra Darkthorn, and each beast he sets before them carries its own lesson: the savage Ishamuhale, the thunder lizards, the thunderhawk. To those who bring him tokens of legendary beasts like Lakota'mani the Earthshaker or Washte Pawne, he explains their meaning: Washte Pawne teaches that regret turns to wisdom. When a pupil has learned all he can teach, he sends them on: to his sister Mahren on the coast, to Ashenvale, or to Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff.

Warriors of the Horde seek him out for his weapons, and for those whose deeds have grown famous he will forge a suit of brutal armor, a labor so great that he wrote out the materials on a scroll over many nights with his failing eyes and calls on other smiths of the Horde to help.

His other ventures range wider: deepmoss spider eggs from Stonetalon for the omelette craze in Booty Bay, blueleaf tubers sniffed out by trained gophers in Razorfen Kraul, and bogbean leaves from the Dustwallow swamps, fetched by his hired help Stinky Ignatz.

title: The Demon Seed
body: Hunting the Burning Blade through Durotar, the Horde learned from the warlock Neeru Fireblade that the cult rallies around an object of demonic power, the Demon Seed, kept atop Dreadmist Peak in the Barrens. Neeru, who claims to have searched out demonic corruption among the orcs ever since the Burning Legion was defeated in the last great war, wants it destroyed. The Seed is a tool of the Legion itself, resting in a cave above an altar of demonic fire, and the cultists of the Burning Blade guard the slopes around it. To learn how it can be undone, Neeru sends the hero west to his assistant Ak'Zeloth at Far Watch Post, on the border of the Barrens.

parts.body: Ak'Zeloth found Neeru's order strange, but he obeyed. He had prepared power stones that, set near the Seed, would disrupt its connection to the Legion: flawed stones whose power consumes itself in time. One had to be taken from his table and carried in haste up the safer northern face of the peak, past the cultists, to the altar of fire.
sources: quest 809 reward text (Strange...)
quest 924 description and objectives

parts.body: The stone did its work, and the Demon Seed was destroyed. This was not the end, Ak'Zeloth warned: its destruction sent waves of staggering force through the ether, waves he was sure other beings had felt as well, others who would wonder why their toy had been broken. Then he paid the hero with what Neeru had sent, and Neeru's thanks.
sources: quest 924 reward text

title: Kranal Fiss and the Call of Fire
body: When a young orc, troll or tauren shaman has learned patience in the ways of earth, the trainers of Razor Hill, Orgrimmar, Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff decide it is time for a greater test. The element of fire, they say, can be theirs if they are prepared to pay for it, and they send the novice north of the Crossroads to Kranal Fiss at Grol'dom Farm, a shaman strong in the ways of the elements. The farm is easy to find, the trainers warn, so long as one does not go too far: keep on past it and the road runs into the lands of the night elves.

parts.body: Kranal sees the burning desire in a novice's eyes. Power and destruction will come easily, he warns, but one must still know when to stay one's hand. Then he hands over a torch that marks an attempt to tame fire, to be carried to Telf Joolam, keeper of the Shrine of the Dormant Flame in Durotar, and brought back aflame.

quest 1524 description

parts.body: The keeper asked for two things to make the fire sapta: fire tar, carried by the Razormane spellcasters of the eastern Barrens, and a reagent pouch taken from the Burning Blade, for a sapta is always made from things bound to its element. When they were brought he taught that fire is not only chaos and destruction but life and creation, each force giving the other meaning.
sources: quest 1525 description, request and reward text

parts.body: When the torch came back lit from the shrine, Kranal saw a spirit that burned brighter than any torch he had ever seen. If the novice keeps to this path, he said, the elements will be theirs to command and their brethren will look to them for guidance and wisdom, and he presented the novice's newest totem.

title: Islen Waterseer and the Call of Water
body: Shamans of the Horde whose spirits are warmed by fire are sent to Islen Waterseer at her fishing hut south of Ratchet. Her lesson is simple: water means rebirth, healing and cleansing when it is pure, but when polluted it devastates all it touches. For the sapta she sends them deep into the south to the shaman Brine, who lives alone on Blackthorn Ridge among hostile quilboar. Brine asks for three samples of the purest water: from the pond below her hut, which the quilboar guard as a sacred hoard, from a fresh well in the Forsaken town of Tarren Mill, a holy vestige in an unhallowed sea, and from the fountain at the Ruins of Stardust in Ashenvale.

title: The Oases of the Barrens
body: The druids of Thunder Bluff sense a strange power leaking into the Barrens, and Tonga Runetotem was sent to the Crossroads to find its source. Once lush and teeming with life, the land was scorched to a dry husk by war and upheaval long ago, yet within the past few years new oases have formed and life is stirring again. Deep down, the druids feel a power working its way to the surface. Tonga cannot unravel the mystery alone, and he begins with the Forgotten Pools northwest of the Crossroads, whose waters he wants searched for the source of that power.

parts.body: At the bottom of the Forgotten Pools lies a fissure in the earth with gases bubbling up from it. Tonga called it a clue, not yet an answer, and wondered whether such fissures lie beneath the other oases too, as the source of their life.

quest 877 description

parts.body: One did. At the Stagnant Oasis, dead and dried seeds dropped into a second fissure sprang to life, and Tonga was amazed: whatever rests beneath the oases can create life from nothing. He turned next to the beasts that drink there, and sent hunters after the snapjaw turtles of the Lushwater and Stagnant Oases for their shells.
sources: quest 877 reward text
quest 880 description

parts.body: The shells bore a taint Tonga had never seen. The waters of the oases were its cause, he judged, and they spread a confusion through the land, as if it dreams and cannot wake. The source must be the Wailing Caverns, and before anyone ventured there he sent them to the elder druid Hamuul Runetotem on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise for counsel.
sources: quest 1489 description

parts.body: One shell went further. Tonga's clanmate Mura Runetotem had gone to Silverpine to bring new life to that dying forest, and to her the shell seemed to glow from within, as if it still pulsed with life. She hopes it holds a secret that can help her heal the land.
sources: quest 3301 description and reward text

parts.body: The dreaming of the druids of Thunder Bluff named the culprits: the Druids of the Fang, who lair in the Wailing Caverns. They were once part of a noble order that meant to heal the Barrens, but they have lost their way and now seek to remake the land to match their own twisted dreams. They have four leaders, Cobrahn, Anacondra, Pythas and Serpentis, each holding a dream gem, and even now their faces haunt Nara Wildmane.
sources: quest 914 description
quest 1490 description (cult of druids once noble)

parts.body: The four leaders of the Fang were slain in the depths of the caverns and their gems carried to Nara Wildmane in Thunder Bluff. Her dreams are free of their wicked faces at last, and she gives thanks for herself, for the druids of Thunder Bluff and for the land, which has been spared a cursed future.
sources: quest 914 reward text

title: The Kolkar Leaders
body: The Kolkar centaurs have plagued the tauren for years, but in the Barrens they were disorganized until new leaders rose among them and rallied them into a real threat. From his bunkers west of the Crossroads, Regthar Deathgate means to destroy those leaders one by one, and he pays a bounty on every centaur bracer brought in. First is Barak Kodobane, who camps near the Forgotten Pools. After him come Verog the Dervish, who roams the plains from the command tent at the Stagnant Oasis, and Hezrul Bloodmark, leader of all the Kolkar in the Barrens, who commands from the Lushwater Oasis. Regthar also recruits agents to carry the fight into Desolace, the Kolkar homeland.

They are undisciplined, Regthar says, and cannot focus their rage as the orcs can, but they are fierce nonetheless.
sources: quest 852 description and reward text

parts.body: The Kolkar answered in fury. A war band came out of Desolace to seek vengeance and fell upon Regthar's bunkers from the west. Only when their warlord Krom'zar was slain and a piece of his banner taken did the attack break, and Regthar promised that Thrall himself would hear of the victory.

title: The Hunt of the Barrens
body: Young hunters come to the Crossroads to learn that there is more to the hunt than finding and killing. Sergra Darkthorn starts them on the plainstriders that harass the town's food supplies and on the strong-legged zhevra, then on the sly prowlers of the tall grass, and then on Echeyakee, Whitemist, king of the savannah cats, called to his lair among the kodo bones with a horn; the tauren say he is both mercy and death. Next she has them take the feathers of slain sunscale raptors and lay them on the scytheclaw nests, to show the beasts' kin they are not afraid.

title: Betrayal from Within
body: Razormane raids on the caravans from Durotar are starving the Crossroads, and Thork wants them stopped. His scouts are hunting the leader of the raids, and one name has come back: the raider Kreenig Snarlsnout, seen northeast of the town. Another account comes from an unlikely mouth. In a cage at Camp Taurajo sits Mangletooth, a Razormane prisoner who claims to know who really causes Thork such anguish. He offers a bargain: strike the Bristlebacks, the Razormane's rivals, by killing their spiritual leaders to the north, and he will tell. He speaks too of Agamaggan, the boar god whose blood raised the thorns, and of the blood shards the Bristlebacks dig from the earth.

parts.body: Kreenig Snarlsnout died and his tusk was carried back as proof, and Thork expected a sure decline in the attacks on his caravans. Cut off the head of their leader, he taught, and chaos follows: the boars would flounder without direction.

parts.body: Mangletooth kept his word and gave up his own kin. Three of his tribe came out of the Kraul to lead the raids against the Horde, he said: the caster Nak, the tracker Kuz and their leader, the warrior Lok Orcbane, far to the south. Kill them, he said, and the Crossroads will know peace from the Razormane.
sources: quest 879 description

parts.body: The skulls of all three were brought back to his cage. Better it ends this way, Mangletooth said; they should have made sure he was dead before they turned their backs on him. One task remained: Lok Orcbane's skull was to go to Thork, who would understand what had happened without a word.
sources: quest 879 reward text
quest 906 description

parts.body: Thork, who had been so sure the raids were led by another quilboar, was left without words when the skull was laid before him. He had never imagined who his true foe was. He gave his thanks and bid the people of the Crossroads respect such strength.
sources: quest 906 reward text

title: The Samophlange
body: Sputtervalve of the Tinkers' Union is already in hot water over the shredder program Director Riddlevox put in his charge, and the Union's deadlines are not the sort to miss. Now he has learned that the Venture Company is experimenting with something called a samophlange at a small research site far to the north, southwest of the Sludge Fen. No one can say what a samophlange is, which only makes him want it more. He has even obtained a copy of the site's control system operating manual, and with it, he reckons, the device can be disengaged from its console and brought to him.

Wenikee Boltbucket, a clever tinkerer camped south of Mor'shan, was thrilled to see it, but the extra gauges she fitted read its integrity at an all time low, and more dials might only make it worse. She sent it to Rilli Greasygob of Orgrimmar, who once worked for the Venture Company.

title: Deep Cover
body: The Shattered Hand has spent a year planting an agent deep inside the Venture Company, and at last word has come from him: the goblins are planning something on a grand scale. Shenthul sends a trusted rogue north of the Sludge Fen to the company's tower to make contact with the agent, Taskmaster Fizzule. The instructions are strict. Once the tower is in sight, two flares must be fired from the gun Shenthul provides, and then the Shattered Salute given, in that order, for Fizzule will attack and kill anyone he does not recognize.

Now the rogue must steal the tower key from Foreman Silixiz, cut down its drones, patrollers and lookouts, assassinate Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix and pick his lockbox for a cache of Zanzil's altered mixture.

Gallywix's head and the cache of Zanzil's mixture went back to Shenthul in Orgrimmar, who spoke of poor Fizzule, a good agent and one of the Hand's best. Being a field agent of the Shattered Hand is dangerous work, he said, and that is the price they pay.
